set.body: Reorganize the project wiki so anyone — a new developer, a PM, an auditor — can find the right page and know whether it is current or historical. Adds a formal content model, stable page identities, truth-state banners, generated navigation and indexes, and an evidence chain from plans to releases. The full design lives in the plan doc; work proceeds in phases, foundations first.
set.title: IA & content model (supersedes wiki-information-architecture)

set.body: Turn the remaining warnings into hard CI failures, add sidebar/navigation rendering for GitLab, Azure DevOps, and Confluence wikis, and add a search command over the doc inventory.
set.title: Phase 5: promote gates to hard fail; platform render adapters (GitLab/ADO/Confluence); /worklog:find + glossary

set.body: Extend the item model beyond the fixed core (id/title/status/level/kind/milestone/priority) with a configurable optional-field set, so lightweight and heavyweight processes share one log. Config block (work_item_fields in .work/config.yml) enables fields per team; every enabled field carries a description so humans AND agents use it correctly; disabled fields never appear in prompts, forms, or validation. Recommended default-on: priority, estimate, risk, owner, milestone, acceptance_criteria, labels. Default-off: value, confidence, due_date, severity, time tracking. Dependencies stay typed (blocked_by/blocks, relates_to) and feed the Traceability Index. Design principles: small stable core; explicit documented options; conservative defaults; process-agnostic. Full spec discussed 2026-07-22; re-derive the detailed field table when this is planned.
set.title: Configurable work-item field model: optional fields (estimate, risk, effort, value, confidence, owner, due_date, acceptance_criteria, blocked_by/blocks) behind work_item_fields config

set.body: worklog close and worklog update look up the item by exact dict key (fold(...).items.get(a.item) / base(a.item, ...)) instead of resolving prefixes the way worklog reopen already does (id.startswith(a.item)). Passing an 8-char prefix — the normal form worklog show/list output and the docs recommend — silently writes a new orphan phantom item under the short id instead of erroring or resolving to the real item; on update it also skips taxonomy validation since the current-state lookup silently returns {}. Reproduced live: 'worklog close 01KYA8MD' (valid prefix of 01KYA8MDY5HP9MC5KQMJX3BN84) created an orphan closed item instead of closing the real one. Fix: give close/update the same prefix-resolution + not-found error that reopen already has.
set.title: close/update silently corrupt log when given an item-id prefix instead of the full ULID

set.body: Give every ticket, PR, and release its own generated wiki page reusing the IA content model's wiki_key/truth_state/traceability-graph machinery already built for docs — so a reader sees hierarchy, related artifacts, and traceability in one place instead of hunting indexes/logs.
set.title: Extend IA to tickets, PRs, and releases (artifact pages)

set.body: The release skill requires a hand-written '## X.Y.Z — unreleased' CHANGELOG section before a release can be cut, but nothing enforces writing it as features land — v0.13.0's section had to be manually reconstructed from 'git log v0.12.1..HEAD' after 36 commits piled up unlogged. Have the release skill (or a new 'worklog changelog-draft' step) generate a starting draft of the unreleased section from git log since the last tag, grouped by the existing commit-prefix convention (feat/fix/chore), excluding pure worklog housekeeping commits — a human/agent still reviews and edits the prose before stamping, but the 'we forgot to write it' failure mode goes away.
set.title: Auto-draft the release CHANGELOG unreleased section from git log

set.body: bin/ia_render.py's banner() (~line 68) returns the 'the latest %s report' text for ANY doc that is truth_state:current AND frozen (ia.is_frozen()) — but is_frozen() is true for plan/roadmap-snapshot/status/dated-design, not just status reports, and the message hardcodes rec.get('kind','status') which plans never set. Verified live: 12 of 14 plan/* entries in docs/.index/publish-manifest.json carry the banner 'the latest status report. Reports freeze once published...' even though they are plans, not status reports. Fix: branch on rec['doc_type'] == 'status' specifically, and give frozen-but-current plans their own correct banner text (e.g. 'the current plan; plans are frozen once written, a changed design gets a new plan').
set.title: banner() mislabels frozen 'current' plans as status reports

set.body: PR pages (docs/.index/rendered/prs/<N>.md, from render_pr_page() in bin/ia_render.py) currently show files-changed and test/review status as 'not tracked' -- deliberately deferred out of the artifact-pages epic since no code in this repo fetches gh pr view data today. Add 'worklog pr-sync <num>': one gh pr view <num> --json title,url,state,files,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,mergedAt call, written via the already-generic ia.write_sidecar('pr/<num>', {...}) (same pattern as link_pr() in bin/ia_graph.py). Must stay outside render_all() to preserve the network-free render invariant -- a manual/CI step, not part of every render. render_pr_page() already degrades gracefully without it.
set.title: worklog pr-sync: fetch live PR metadata (files, review/CI status)

set.body: sync_dispatch.py's pull step calls the adapter with no --since/--keys when .work/sync-state.json has no 'cursors' entry yet for a repo -- but the adapter's own contract requires one of --since <iso> or --keys, so the very first pull always fails (exit 1: 'pull requires --since <iso> or --keys'). Surfaced during a routine 'worklog sync' run in wiki_ticket_sdd itself -- not specific to any feature, a general first-pull gap. Fix: seed a --since on the first pull (e.g. repo creation date, or the earliest local event timestamp) when no cursor exists yet, instead of calling the adapter with neither.
set.title: worklog sync --pull can never bootstrap: cursor-less pull calls the adapter with no --since, which it requires

set.body: bin/ia_graph.py's build_graph() only creates a 'lands-in' edge when an item sidecar's code entry has a 'pr' key (c.get('pr') is not None) -- a commit-only entry ({'commit': '<sha>'}, written by worklog link-pr --commit with no --pr) creates no edge at all, so trace-check --strict still reports 'no PR/commit link' even after linking a real commit. Hit twice now: v0.13.0's release PR (direct-to-main landings, no PR) and v0.14.0's artifact-pages epic (same pattern -- 11 items linked via --commit, all still flagged). Fix: also create a lands-in edge (to a commit/<sha> node, or similar) when only 'commit' is set.
set.title: ia_graph build_graph() ignores commit-only sidecar code links (lands-in only honors code.pr)

set.body: bin/sync_dispatch.py push_items(): the scope skip ('closed and not ext.get("key") and not forced: continue') is correctly bypassed when --keys forces the item in, but the closed-item branch unconditionally reads ext['key'] (both the dry-run print and the real close() call), assuming a closed item always already has an external key. A closed item that was NEVER pushed (no external.key) and is forced into scope via --keys crashes with KeyError: 'key' instead of create-then-close. Repro: bin/worklog sync --dry-run --keys <ulid-of-closed-never-remote-item>. Hit while reconciling 01KYAH3VHPSEK2RY63J7Y109FR (release item, done, never remote) during v0.14.0 wiki/ticket publish; worked around by manually running the adapter's create step + worklog link before syncing, so the item enters the already-working closed+ext.key path. Fix: in the closed branch, if not ext.get('key'), do create-then-close (mirror the non-closed create path) instead of assuming update-then-close.
set.title: sync_dispatch push_items KeyError on ext['key'] when forcing a never-remote closed item into scope via --keys

set.body: New git hooks (shipped in the plugin) that block authored commits directly on main/master and require every commit message to reference a worklog item or ticket -- prevents the local/origin main-drift incident that broke a release PR merge this session.
set.title: Branch-discipline hooks: never commit on main, always reference work
